stories.title: Presidents Cup Sunday Singles — International Team on Verge of Historic Win

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
The International Team enters Presidents Cup Sunday singles leading 10.5-7.5.

They've NEVER won on American soil. Never won away from Australia since 1998.

They need 5 points from 12 singles.

This could be the most historic day in Presidents Cup history. 🏆 #PresidentsCup

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Presidents Cup Sunday singles scorecard heading in:

🌏 International: 10.5
🇺🇸 USA: 7.5

Internationals need just 5 more points.
USA needs 8 of 12.

Scottie Scheffler vs Nico Echavarria is the headliner.

History on the line at Medinah. #PresidentsCup

facebook.long_form:
The most important day in Presidents Cup history is happening RIGHT NOW.

The International Team heads into Sunday singles at Medinah Country Club with a 10.5–7.5 lead over the United States — the first time in the event's 32-year history that the Internationals have held a lead on American soil heading into the final day.

The math is simple: Internationals need 5 points from 12 singles matches. USA needs to win 8 of 12 to retain the cup.

The International Team has never won on foreign soil. Their last (and only) victory was at Royal Melbourne in 1998. They've lost 12 consecutive times since. Today could end all of that.

The singles lineups feature some of the biggest names in golf:
• Scottie Scheffler vs. Nico Echavarria
• Chris Gotterup and Cameron Young (US bright spots — both went 2-0 on Saturday)

A win for the Internationals would be one of the greatest upsets in the history of the event — and it would happen on American soil, at Medinah, the same course where Europe staged their 2012 Ryder Cup comeback from 10-6 down.

History doesn't repeat. But sometimes it rhymes. 🏆
facebook.image_caption: International Team: 10.5. USA: 7.5. Sunday singles at Medinah. The Internationals need FIVE more points to make history. 🌏🏆 #PresidentsCup

stories.title: NW Arkansas Championship — Nishimura Leads by 5 in Final Round

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Yuna Nishimura enters the final round of the NW Arkansas Championship leading by FIVE shots at -16.

She shot back-to-back rounds of 63. Matched the 36-hole tournament scoring record.

She has 6 wins in Japan. Zero on the LPGA Tour. Today could change that. 🏌️‍♀️ #LPGA

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
The chase group at NW Arkansas entering the final round:

T2: Auston Kim (-11)
T2: Mary Liu (-11)
T2: Michelle Zhang (-11, rookie)

All five shots behind Yuna Nishimura.

Can anyone close the gap? 🏌️‍♀️ #LPGA #NWArkansas

facebook.long_form:
Yuna Nishimura is 18 holes away from her first LPGA Tour victory.

The 26-year-old from Japan entered Sunday's final round at Pinnacle Country Club in Rogers, Arkansas with a five-shot lead at -16, having shot back-to-back rounds of 8-under 63. Her 36-hole score matched the tournament's all-time scoring record.

Nishimura has six victories on the Japan LPGA Tour but has never won on the LPGA Tour circuit. Zero wins in four seasons. The opportunity is right in front of her.

Standing between her and history: Auston Kim, Mary Liu, and LPGA rookie Michelle Zhang — all tied at -11, five shots back.

Five-shot leads with 18 holes to play are rarely squandered in golf. But in tournament conditions, with a first win on the line, nerves become a factor no leaderboard can predict.

Will Yuna Nishimura break through today? 🏌️‍♀️
facebook.image_caption: Yuna Nishimura leads by FIVE with 18 to play at NW Arkansas. Back-to-back 63s. Seeking her first LPGA Tour win. Today's the day? 🏌️‍♀️ #LPGA

stories.title: LIV Golf — BC Partners $300M Deal, Oct. 13 Player Commitment Deadline

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text:
LIV Golf's rescue plan:

• BC Partners: $300M for "LIV 2.0"
• Players become majority owners
• 2027 relaunch target

Oct. 13 deadline: player commitment required.

Rahm ($7.5M) and DeChambeau ($5.8M) owed.

Clock is ticking. #LIVGolf

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text:
October 13 is the most important date in LIV Golf history.

Players representing 2/3 of total claim value must commit to the restructuring or the BC Partners rescue deal falls apart.

Jon Rahm. Bryson DeChambeau. Cameron Smith. Dustin Johnson.

What do they choose? #LIVGolf

facebook.long_form:
LIV Golf's future is now in the hands of its players — and there are 16 days to decide.

Here's the full picture of where things stand:

📌 September 8: LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey federal court. Total liabilities: $500 million to $1 billion. The trigger: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund pulled its backing.

💰 The rescue deal: London-based private equity firm BC Partners is offering $300 million to fund a restructured "LIV 2.0" where players would become majority owners. The Saudi PIF agreed to provide $49.6 million in temporary financing to keep the lights on during the process.

⏰ The deadline: October 13. Players representing at least two-thirds of total claim value AND at least half of total claim count must commit to the restructuring — or the deal collapses.

💵 What players are owed: Jon Rahm is the largest creditor at approximately $7.5 million. Bryson DeChambeau is owed approximately $5.8 million. Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith are also listed as unsecured creditors. Total owed to players: approximately $45 million.

🚪 The PGA Tour: Closed the return window. No pathway currently for LIV players.

The question is whether Rahm, DeChambeau, Smith, and the rest will bet on themselves by committing to LIV 2.0 — or walk away from the money they're owed and try to find another path forward.

October 13 is 16 days away. Comment below — do you think LIV 2.0 will actually happen? 👇
facebook.image_caption: LIV Golf Chapter 11: $300M BC Partners rescue. Oct. 13 player commitment deadline. Rahm owed $7.5M. DeChambeau $5.8M. The clock is ticking on LIV 2.0. ⏰ #LIVGolf

facebook.long_form:
The Presidents Cup wraps up today at Medinah — and the PGA Tour is ready to pivot immediately.

Tomorrow, the second event of the FedEx Cup Fall series begins:

**Bank of Utah Championship**
📍 Black Desert Resort, Utah
📅 September 28 – October 4
🏆 8-event FedEx Cup Fall series

The fall schedule is about survival. Players who don't hold a PGA Tour card for 2027 need strong performances across these eight events to secure full status.

After the Bank of Utah, the Tour heads to Japan for the Baycurrent Classic (October 5-11) and then the Butterfield Bermuda Championship. Two of the eight fall events are entirely new for 2026 — including the Biltmore Championship in Asheville that kicked off the series.

Golf doesn't stop. Who are you watching at Black Desert? ⛳

stories.title: Lauren Coughlin's Nine-Birdie Streak — LPGA Tour Record

x_posts.label: Post 5-1
x_posts.text:
Lauren Coughlin opened Round 2 at the NW Arkansas Championship with NINE consecutive birdies.

Nine. In a row.

An LPGA Tour record.

And she wasn't even the story of the day — Yuna Nishimura shot 63 to lead by 5. What a tournament. 🏌️‍♀️ #LPGA

x_posts.label: Post 5-2
x_posts.text:
Lauren Coughlin's 9-birdie run in perspective:

• LPGA record — most consecutive birdies to start a round
• Saturday, Pinnacle CC, Arkansas
• Historic pace. Still couldn't catch Nishimura.

Golf at Pinnacle this week was absurd. #LPGA #LPGARecord

facebook.long_form:
Nine consecutive birdies to open a round. That's what Lauren Coughlin did at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship on Saturday.

Nine. In a row.

It is an LPGA Tour record — the most consecutive birdies from the start of a round in the tournament's history.

The remarkable part? Coughlin's historic start didn't even put her in the lead. Yuna Nishimura was so dominant this week that Coughlin's nine consecutive birdies still left her chasing.

That's how exceptional the scoring has been at Pinnacle Country Club in Rogers, Arkansas this week. Low numbers everywhere — but one player, Nishimura, managed to be 5 shots better than everyone else.

History was made in both Round 2 performances — and only one of them is being talked about as the lead story. Sometimes golf is just like that.

If nine consecutive birdies was YOUR headline weekend, you'd want people to remember it! Let us know — what's the most memorable golf record you can think of? 👇 ⛳
facebook.image_caption: Lauren Coughlin opened Round 2 with NINE consecutive birdies — an LPGA Tour record. And she still wasn't leading the tournament. What a week at NW Arkansas. ⛳ #LPGA #LPGARecord
